newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Presidential guards arrested in Burkina - paper.
newsitem.headline: Presidential guards arrested in Burkina - paper.

text.p: Seventeen soldiers of Burkina Faso's presidential guard have been arrested for acts of indiscipline, the official daily Sidwaya reported on Tuesday.
It said all 17 were close to the former head of President Blaise Compaore's security, sub-officer Hyacinthe Kafando, who is on a training course in Morocco.

The newspaper described Kafando, who is said to be close to Compaore, as a "feared officer" who led his men into "acts contrary to military discipline". Military authorities appear to have taken advantage of his absence to arrest his men.
The newspaper said Kafando demanded in a report from his course that he expected to be made a full officer on his return.
"The arrests were of a preventive nature to avert a settling of scores in this specialised unit of the army," it added.
Members of the presidential security are from the National Commando Training Centre in the southern town of Po, which was once commanded by Compaore.
The head of state will next week mark the ninth anniversary of his taking power following a coup on October 1987 in which then president Captain Thomas Sankara was killed.
